## About Visa Service Phuket

Visa Service Phuket is a local visa support service based in Wichit, Phuket, Thailand. We help foreigners living in or visiting Phuket with Thai visa extensions, retirement visa support, Non-Immigrant visa guidance, DTV visa guidance, 90-day reports, re-entry permits, TM30 address notifications, and Thai driving license conversion at the DLT.

We are a guidance and document preparation service — we do not make immigration decisions and cannot guarantee visa approval. We review each person's situation, explain available options in plain language, provide a clear document checklist, and guide the appointment process at Phuket Immigration or the DLT.

## How it works (5 steps)

1. **Send us your situation** — Share your nationality, current visa type and what you need. A quick WhatsApp message is enough.
2. **We check your options** — We review your case and explain which route fits, in plain language.
3. **You prepare the documents** — You get a clear checklist so nothing is missing on the day.
4. **We guide you step by step** — We walk you through the process and answer questions as they come up.
5. **You complete the appointment** — You attend prepared and confident, knowing what to expect.

## Services

### Visa Extension in Phuket
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/visa-extension-phuket/

Most visas in Thailand can be extended at Phuket Immigration in Wichit — if your paperwork is right and you go before your current permission to stay runs out. Tourist visas, visa exemptions and most Non-Immigrant categories (Non-O for retirement, marriage, family and more) can usually be extended.

**Documents usually needed:**
- Passport with the current visa or entry stamp
- TM30 (proof-of-address notification)
- Completed TM7 extension form and a photo
- Supporting documents for your reason (financial proof, marriage or retirement evidence)

**FAQ:**
- Q: Can I extend a tourist visa in Phuket?
  A: In many cases yes — a tourist visa or visa exemption can usually be extended once at Phuket Immigration. The extra time granted depends on current rules and your situation.
- Q: Do I need a TM30 to extend my visa?
  A: Usually yes. A valid TM30 address notification is commonly required for extensions. We check whether yours is in order and help you update it if needed.
- Q: How long does a visa extension take in Phuket?
  A: Many extensions are handled in a single appointment if your documents are complete. Processing can vary with Immigration workload — we give you a realistic expectation.
- Q: What if my visa already expired?
  A: Contact us as soon as possible. You may face an overstay fine, but acting quickly usually keeps your options open.

---

### Retirement Visa Support in Phuket
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/retirement-visa-phuket/

Thailand offers long-stay options for retirees aged 50 and over, primarily through the Non-Immigrant O or O-A visa categories. Which route fits depends on where you apply, your financial situation and whether you already hold a Thai visa.

**Common requirements:**
- Age 50 or older at time of application
- Financial evidence (bank deposit, income or a combination — exact thresholds depend on the category and current rules)
- Medical clearance and, in some cases, qualifying health insurance
- A valid TM30 address notification in Phuket

**FAQ:**
- Q: What is the cheapest way to get a retirement visa in Phuket?
  A: Cost depends on your current visa, financial situation and which route you take. We compare the options and explain what each involves so you can decide.
- Q: Can I apply for a retirement visa at Phuket Immigration?
  A: Yes. We help with the documents and guide your appointment at Phuket Immigration for the one-year extension of stay.
- Q: Do I need health insurance for a retirement visa?
  A: Some retirement routes (especially O-A) can require qualifying health insurance. We tell you whether it applies to your case.

---

### Non-Immigrant Visa Guidance in Phuket
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/non-immigrant-visa-phuket/

Non-Immigrant visas cover a range of categories — O (retirement, marriage, family), O-A (long-stay retirement from abroad), B (business/work) and ED (education). Which category fits depends on your reason for staying in Thailand.

**FAQ:**
- Q: Which Non-Immigrant visa do I need?
  A: It depends on your reason to stay — retirement, marriage, work or study each map to a different category. Tell us your situation and we match the right one.
- Q: Can I change to a Non-Immigrant visa inside Thailand?
  A: In some cases a change of visa type or status is possible within Thailand; in others you apply from abroad. We explain which applies to you.
- Q: Do you guarantee the visa will be approved?
  A: No service can guarantee Immigration approval. We help you understand the requirements and prepare your documents correctly.

---

### DTV Visa Guidance in Phuket (Destination Thailand Visa)
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/dtv-visa-phuket/

The DTV (Destination Thailand Visa) is a long-validity Thai visa for remote workers, freelancers and people joining qualifying activities in Thailand. It is typically applied for at a Thai embassy or consulate abroad.

**FAQ:**
- Q: What is the DTV visa?
  A: The Destination Thailand Visa is a long-validity Thai visa for remote workers, freelancers and people joining qualifying activities in Thailand.
- Q: Can I get the DTV while in Phuket?
  A: The DTV is typically applied for at a Thai embassy or consulate. We help you understand the process and prepare your documents.
- Q: Is the DTV right for me, or should I use another visa?
  A: It depends on your work, finances and plans. We compare the DTV against options like Non-O or extensions so you choose the best fit.

---

### 90-Day Report in Phuket
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/90-day-report-phuket/

Every foreigner staying in Thailand on a long-stay visa must report their current address to Immigration every 90 days. This is separate from a visa extension and carries a 2,000 THB fine if missed.

**Methods:** In person at Phuket Immigration, online (when the system accepts it), or with assistance.

**FAQ:**
- Q: Is the 90-day report the same as a visa extension?
  A: No. The 90-day report only confirms your address. Your visa or extension of stay is a separate matter with its own dates.
- Q: What happens if I miss my 90-day report?
  A: Missing it typically means a fine (commonly 2,000 THB). It does not count as overstay or create an entry ban.
- Q: Can I do the 90-day report online in Phuket?
  A: Online filing is available in many cases. If the system rejects your report, an in-person visit to Phuket Immigration is needed.

---

### Re-Entry Permit in Phuket
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/re-entry-permit-phuket/

A re-entry permit keeps your Thai extension of stay valid when you leave Thailand temporarily. Without one, your extension is cancelled on departure — even for a weekend trip.

**Types:** Single re-entry (one trip) or multiple re-entry (unlimited trips until your stay expires).

**FAQ:**
- Q: Do I need a re-entry permit for a short trip?
  A: Yes — any departure without one cancels your extension of stay, even for a weekend trip.
- Q: Can I get a re-entry permit at Phuket airport?
  A: Often yes, at the Immigration desk before departure, but queues can be tight. Getting it in advance at Phuket Immigration is safer.
- Q: Single or multiple re-entry permit — which is better?
  A: If you travel once, single is enough. If you fly several times before your stay ends, a multiple permit is usually more practical.

---

### Thai Driving License in Phuket
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/thai-driving-license-phuket/

Foreigners with a valid foreign driving license can convert it to a Thai driving license at the Phuket Department of Land Transport (DLT). A Thai license is legally required for driving in Thailand.

**FAQ:**
- Q: Can I convert my foreign driving license in Phuket?
  A: Often yes. With a valid foreign license or IDP plus the right documents, you can usually obtain a Thai license at the Phuket DLT.
- Q: Do I need a residence certificate for a Thai driving license?
  A: Usually yes — proof of address from Phuket Immigration or your embassy is commonly required.
- Q: Do I need to take a test?
  A: If your foreign license is recognised, you typically skip the practical test but still complete the short physical checks and reaction test.
- Q: How long is a first Thai driving license valid?
  A: A first Thai license is usually issued as a two-year license, then renewable for longer periods.

---

### TM30 Address Notification in Phuket
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/tm30-phuket/

The TM30 is a notification of address that Thai law requires when a foreigner stays at any address. Legally the property owner or landlord files it, but in practice the foreigner often has to arrange it. A valid TM30 is required for most visa-related applications at Phuket Immigration.

**FAQ:**
- Q: Who is responsible for filing the TM30?
  A: Legally the property owner, landlord or hotel files it, but in practice the foreigner often has to chase it.
- Q: Do I need a new TM30 after travelling?
  A: Often yes — returning from abroad or changing address can require an updated TM30.
- Q: Can a missing TM30 stop my visa extension?
  A: Yes. Phuket Immigration commonly requires a valid TM30 before processing extensions or 90-day reports.

---

### Phuket Immigration Office — Visitor Guide
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/phuket-immigration-office/

The main Phuket Immigration office is located in Tambon Wichit, Mueang Phuket District. It handles visa extensions, 90-day reports, re-entry permits, TM30 notifications, and other immigration matters for foreigners in Phuket.

**FAQ:**
- Q: Where is Phuket Immigration located?
  A: The main Phuket Immigration office is in Tambon Wichit, Mueang Phuket District.
- Q: What are Phuket Immigration opening hours?
  A: Government offices generally open on weekdays during business hours and close on public holidays. Hours can change, so confirm before your visit.
- Q: Can you go to Immigration with me?
  A: We prepare your documents and guide you through the process, and can support you on the day so your visit goes smoothly.
- Q: Why was my application refused at Immigration?
  A: Common reasons are a missing or outdated TM30, unsigned copies, or incomplete evidence. We pre-check everything to avoid this.

## Free Online Tools

### Thailand Visa Overstay Fine Calculator
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/tools/overstay-calculator/
The overstay fine in Thailand is 500 THB per day, capped at 20,000 THB. Longer overstays can lead to re-entry bans.

### Thailand 90-Day Report Due-Date Calculator
URL: https://phuketvisaservice.com/tools/90-day-report-calculator/
The 90-day report is due 90 days after your last report or entry. You can file from 15 days before to 7 days after the due date. Late filing is commonly fined 2,000 THB.

## Important disclaimers

- No visa service can guarantee immigration approval. We help you understand requirements, prepare documents correctly, and guide you through the process.
- Requirements may vary depending on visa type, personal situation, and current Thai immigration rules.
- A valid TM30 (notification of residence) is commonly required for visa-related applications in Phuket.
- Overstay fines and re-entry ban thresholds can change. Always confirm current rules.
- This content is informational guidance, not legal advice.
